strengths: Top-2 label and explicit reasoning identify L6b/subplate excitatory neurons
Correctly weighs NPFFR2, SEMA3E, SEMA3D, HCRTR2, DPP4, FOXP2, GRM4 as L6b/deep-layer markers
weaknesses: Top-1 raw label is not layer-specific
Automated mapping was flagged ambiguous for the raw label
Candidate set contains unrelated classes, although these were not used in the final reasoning

strengths: Neuronal identity is strongly supported by the marker list and enrichment terms
Top-2 candidate correctly proposes L6b glutamatergic cortical neuron
weaknesses: Top-1 label is too broad and omits the directly supported glutamatergic and L6b/cortical components
Less informative than the available subtype resolution

strengths: Uses absence of GABAergic and glial markers to exclude alternative lineages
Deep-layer excitatory markers SEMA3E, SEMA3D, DCHS2, ADAMTSL1 are recognized
weaknesses: Stops at glutamatergic neuron and does not refine to L6b/cortical subtype
Does not leverage NPFFR2/DPP4/HCRTR2 L6b specificity

supporting: DEGs NPFFR2, SEMA3E, SEMA3D, HCRTR2, DPP4, TRPM3, ASIC2, GRM4, FOXP2, CDH6, ITGA8 directly support the added L6b/cortical/glutamatergic components of CL:4023038
Absence of GAD1/GAD2/SST/PVALB and OLIG1/GFAP supports excitatory neuronal rather than GABAergic or glial identity
Pipeline-provided PMIDs 35474380, 38957312, 41388235, 32061372, 40876929, 32508047, 40640508, 39769001 accompany the L6b/deep-layer excitatory neuron interpretation
conflicting: GRM4 is present but SLC17A-family vesicular glutamate transporter markers are not listed; glutamatergic assignment therefore rests on the deep-layer excitatory marker constellation and Ex6 enrichment rather than a direct VGLUT marker
ITGA8 and CDH6 are flagged in the epithelial program channel, but in DLPFC L6b context they are established cortical layer markers and do not indicate contamination
enrichment_or_literature: Enrichment terms include innervation, axon extension involved in axon guidance, neuron projection guidance, Semaphorin interactions, Axon guidance, and Nervous system development
Enrichment rationale cites Lake et al.Science.Ex6 excitatory neuron identity
Pipeline literature is consistent with human cortical deep-layer excitatory neuron identity
